text: Show every DAM Policy requirement with its strength, source and the step that meets it.
Give a step-by-step method for each capability with roles, templates and measures.
Offer a route and learning journey for each role, with progress the reader controls.
Let anyone get in touch without an email address being published.
Let readers search everything and filter every list.
Publish the vocabulary, requirements and templates as open data.
Meet WCAG 2.2 AA in light and dark modes, from 320 to 1920 pixels wide.
Work with scripts turned off and load nothing from other sites.
Label every fact with its provenance and keep sources current.
Name roles, never people, and hold no personal data.
Be findable by search engines with accurate descriptions.
Generate every page from one content file and refuse to build on a broken reference.
Show every capability the policy and adjacent guidance need, flagged explicit, implicit or inferred, with a signpost to the section it comes from.
Let organisations assess their maturity against the government model and DAM strands, keep the answers privately and download them.
Link each role in the policy to government professions, framework roles, skills and learning routes.
Help organisations embed the policy in business as usual and in change programmes, with actions they can track.
Help readers find which sector supplements apply to an asset.
Help readers find their way: a share menu on every page, a site map, a user guide with guided tours and tutorials.
Let organisations reuse the content through links, embedding, open data, AI assistants and an MCP server.
Help organisations connect and buy data management tools without lock-in, with open standards and RFI questions.
Signpost the sister portals where they help, naming each and its status, without merging their journeys or copying their content.
Help people who work across the three portals choose where to start, in what order and why, without merging the portals.
Let users take part in research privately, suggest and vote for ideas, and see the roadmap, backlog and how each item is prioritised against government strategy, in the open.
Let teams name people and work email addresses in their own copies of templates, and keep them out of anything published.
Say whether each template is for business as usual, change or both, offer each template on its own, and offer logs used together as one tabbed workbook.
Give the data type, format, cardinality, controlled values and an example for every catalogue record property.
Group each sector supplement's legislation, standards and frameworks by kind, and show how sector standards meet the catalogue standard.
Describe a critical data asset's entities, relationships and authoritative source, with a relationship diagram drawn from the list (issue 18).
Record retention schedule, period and disposal action in the ownership register and catalogue record, from the organisation's own schedule (issue 19).
Give a data sharing agreement template covering lawful basis, legal gateway, retention and ending the sharing, and signpost the gateways (issue 20).
Show governance layers with the roles in each and what each may and may not change (issue 21).
Signpost health confidentiality gateways and medical device rules in the health and care supplement (issue 22).
Give glossary terms and named frameworks, methodologies and standards a tooltip and a link where they are first mentioned on any page, outside headings and existing links.
List each capability's frameworks, methodologies and standards by kind on its Overview, and name the ones that apply at every step.
Drill down from each slice of the DAMA wheel to its activities and tasks where the portal has them, and publish what a fuller drill-down and a data architecture playbook would take (BL-35, BL-36).
Use only GitHub services (Pages, issue forms, Discussions, Actions and releases), plus an optional Microsoft Forms route for private feedback.
